questions.question: For accounts opened from 1995 through 2000 in East Bohemia districts, list each account ID and its statement-issuance frequency.
questions.title: Region and date filters

questions.question: For each account-disposition type other than OWNER found in districts with average salary above 8000 and at most 9000, give the type and the number of distinct associated accounts.
questions.title: Distinct account counts

questions.question: I'm preparing for a client review and want to gauge how indebted our older customers' accounts are, including accounts that never took any loans. Could you give me the average number of loans per account among accounts whose owner was born before 1950? By 'born before 1950' I mean a birth date earlier than 1 January 1950, and all loans should count regardless of when they were approved. Please give me the average rounded to two decimal places, and nothing else.
questions.evidence: The owner of an account is the client with the OWNER disposition; a DISPONENT is a co-holder who does not own it. A loan is a credit granted on the account, recorded with the date it was approved.
questions.title: Zero-inclusive loan averages

questions.question: I want to find out whether our borrowing households from larger population centres transact differently from local ones. For every account at the Prachatice branch that has taken at least one loan, please give me: the account number, the account opening date, the total amount ever borrowed, how many outside bank counterparties the account has transacted with over its entire history, the owner's home district, the population of that district, and a rank of these borrowing households by home-district population from largest to smallest. Note that a counterparty means a particular bank account at another institution, identified by that account number, not by the bank code, and only transfers to or from another bank count — handling cash at our own branch does not involve a counterparty. A household's home district is the district its owner client is registered in, which is not necessarily Prachatice. For the ranking: largest population first, ties share the same rank and the next rank after a tie is skipped, and among households whose home districts have the same population, list the smaller account number first.
questions.evidence: An outside bank counterparty is a bank account at another institution that money was sent to or received from on a transfer transaction. District population is the number of inhabitants of the district.
questions.title: Joins and window ranking

questions.question: For every event in our records that had at least one attendee, I need the amount spent per attendee on bottled drinking water, in dollars and cents rounded to two decimals. Give me one row per event with the event name and that amount; if an attended event had no water purchases, show 0.00, and if two events share a name, list them separately. Include all events regardless of status, across the club's entire history. A purchase that included water along with other items counts fully toward water.
questions.evidence: water: bottled drinking water bought for attendees
questions.title: Spending per attendee

questions.question: For every event in the club's records, can you give me the event name, event date, total amount budgeted for the event, and the number of members who attended it? Please sort the list by event name, then by event date, both in ascending order.
questions.title: Budgets and attendance
